subject: Business Models
title: Revenue Sharing with Employees
description: A 60-second lesson on Revenue Sharing with Employees.

hook.text: Costco pays warehouse workers $18-29/hour, well above competitors. Its employee turnover is 6%—Walmart's is 44%.

buildup.text: Some companies share revenue or profits with employees through bonuses, profit-sharing, or equity grants.

discovery.text: Costco's low turnover saves millions in hiring and training costs. Paying more actually costs less overall.

twist.text: Most companies treat labor as a cost to minimize. Revenue-sharing treats it as an investment that compounds.

climax.text: Revenue sharing aligns employee incentives with company success. It's a business model, not just generosity.

punchline.text: Pay more, save more. 6% vs 44% turnover. Revenue sharing is a model, not a gift.

quiz.question: Why does Costco's higher pay actually reduce costs?
options: Low turnover saves millions in hiring and training expenses

details.summary: Revenue sharing with employees distributes a portion of company revenue or profits directly to workers beyond their base compensation. Models range from profit-sharing bonuses and equity grants to cooperative structures where employees collectively own the business and share in all financial.
details.whyItMatters: Growing income inequality and labor market competition are pushing companies toward sharing economic gains with employees..
takeaways: Companies distribute portions of revenue or profit directly to employees
Shared ownership aligns employee and company incentives for long-term success
Models range from profit bonuses to full cooperative employee ownership

faq.question: What forms does revenue sharing with employees take?
faq.answer: Profit-sharing bonuses distribute a percentage of annual profits. Stock options and equity grants give ownership stakes. Employee stock ownership plans hold shares in trust. Worker cooperatives give equal ownership to all members..

faq.question: What evidence shows revenue sharing improves business outcomes?
faq.answer: Studies show employee-owned companies have 4% higher productivity. Profit-sharing reduces turnover by 10-15%. Cooperative businesses survive longer than traditional ones. Aligned incentives reduce principal-agent problems..
